TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample-Complexity Guarantees for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Establish non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees for KernelSHAP, proving upper bounds on the number of subset evaluations required to achieve a given accuracy. To do so, analyze the regression formulation of KernelSHAP and use techniques fromΕΠ concentration inequalities to derive a relationship between the sample size, the kernel weights, and the desired precision.

TITLE: Temporally Consistent Satellite Image Forecasting using Hierarchical Defrise Transform and Conditional Generative Models
PROPOSAL: Introduce a Hierarchical Defrise Transform (HDT) to hierarchically model and condition temporal evolution in satellite image time series forecasting. HDT aggregates features from multiple time steps and dynamically captures representations of scene change at varying scales. Use a conditional generative model (e.g., conditional DALL-E) conditioned on the learned HDT representations and a detailed history of observed scene changes to generate realistic future satellite images. The generated images are ensured to be temporally consistent with observed trends and changes.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline unconditional DALL-E on satellite images, (2) DALL-E conditioned on traditional temporal convolutional networks (TCN) representations, (3) HDT without the conditional generative model.
COST: 750
PREDICTION: The incorporation of HDT and conditional generation will significantly improve the temporal consistency of generated satellite images. However, analyzing the effects of large amounts of missing data on scene change modeling might be difficult.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Long-Range Temporal Dependency Perspective on Understanding Scene Change Dynamics in Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel graph neural network (GNN) architecture, SceneChangeGNN, to model long-range temporal dependencies in scene change dynamics. SceneChangeGNN incorporates a dynamic graph structure learned from the satellite image time series and captures complex temporal relationships between scene changes. Use SceneChangeGNN to generate informative, compact scene change narratives and to reason about the causality of observed changes.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline SITS description models without graph neural networks, (2) a fixed graph structure variant of SceneChangeGNN, (3) using SceneChangeGNN as a feature extractor for a downstream task (e.g., future SITS forecasting)
COST: 1080 GPU-hrs
PREDICTION: SceneChangeGNN will show improved performance in scene change description and future forecasting tasks, but the dynamic graph structure might be difficult to interpret, and the model may require large amounts of training data to capture complex temporal relationships.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scene Change Explanation through Temporal Abstraction and Perturbation Analysis
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel explanation framework, Temporal Abstraction Explanation (TAE), to provide interpretable explanations for scene changes in satellite image time series. TAE abstracts temporal dependencies and identifies key factors contributing to observed changes through perturbation analysis. Use TAE in conjunction with SceneChangeGNN (Proposal 3) to explain complex scene change dynamics.
CONTROLS: (1) TAE on its own without SceneChangeGNN, (2) using other explanation methods (e.g., feature importance, saliency maps) on SceneChangeGNN, (3) TAE with a different graph neural network architecture
COST: 1260 GPU-hrs
PREDICTION: TAE will provide effective explanations for scene changes, but the explanation process may be computationally expensive and require careful tuning of hyperparameters. The alignment of TAE explanations with human understanding of scene change dynamics will be crucial for model trustworthiness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting: Cross-Domain Adaptation for Enhanced Generalization
PROPOSAL: Investigate transfer learning for improving the generalization of satellite image time series forecasting models across different domains and geographic regions. Introduce a cross-domain adaptation (CDA) framework to learn relevant feature representations and patterns from a source domain (e.g., densely sampled time series data) and adapt them to a target domain (e.g., sparsely sampled time series data). Evaluate the effectiveness of CDA in combination with existing forecasting models (e.g., temporal CNNs, conditional generative models).
CONTROLS: (1) baseline forecasting models without CDA, (2) CDA with a different source domain, (3) CDA with an existing graph neural network architecture
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Transfer learning and CDA will significantly improve the generalization of satellite image time series forecasting models across different domains, but the alignment of pre-trained models with target domain characteristics may be challenging. The exploration of new domains and geographical regions may require careful selection of relevant features and temporal patterns.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE:  Cross-Domain Adaptation for Enhanced Generalization with Alignment of Temporal and Spatial Features
PROPOSAL: Enhance the transfer learning framework for satellite image time series forecasting by incorporating an alignment component that aligns both temporal and spatial features across source and target domains. This alignment will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the domain differences and improve the effectiveness of cross-domain adaptation. Evaluate the proposed alignment component using various feature extraction methods (e.g., convolutional neural networks, graph neural networks) and investigate its impact on the forecasting performance.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline transfer learning without alignment, (2) alignment without transfer learning, (3) different feature extraction methods for alignment
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The alignment of both temporal and spatial features will significantly improve the transfer learning performance, but the alignment process may be computationally expensive and sensitive to hyperparameters. The suitability of different feature extraction methods for alignment will depend on the characteristics of the source and target domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Forecasts using Transfer Learning and Ensemble Methods
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel approach to evaluate the temporal consistency of satellite image forecasts by combining transfer learning and ensemble methods. Use transfer learning to adapt pre-trained models to each individual image, and employ ensemble methods to combine the predictions of multiple models and mitigate individual model errors. Evaluate the effectiveness of this approach in conjunction with existing forecasting models and explore its potential to improve temporal consistency.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline forecasting models without ensemble methods, (2) ensemble methods without transfer learning, (3) different ensemble methods (e.g., bagging, boosting)
COST: 2100
PREDICTION: The combination of transfer learning and ensemble methods will significantly improve the temporal consistency of satellite image forecasts, but the selection of appropriate models and ensemble methods for a specific task can be challenging. The impact of ensemble methods on model robustness and error mitigation will be crucial for predicting long-term trends in satellite image data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multimodal Fusion for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting using Graph Neural Networks and Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel multimodal fusion framework for satellite image time series forecasting that leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) and attention mechanisms to effectively combine multiple modalities (e.g., satellite imagery, climate data, geographical features). Use GNNs to learn the complex relationships between different modalities and attention mechanisms to selectively focus on relevant information for forecasting. Evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on various satellite image time series forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline models without multimodal fusion, (2) different GNN architectures (e.g., Graph Convolutional Networks, Graph Attention Networks), (3) traditional fusion methods (e.g., concatenation, averaging)
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The multimodal fusion approach will improve the forecasting performance on satellite image time series data, but the selection of relevant modalities and attention mechanisms can be challenging. The integration of graphs and attention mechanisms will provide a promising direction for fusion learning, but requires careful tuning of model hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting under Uncertain or Missing Data using Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel multi-task learning framework for satellite image time series forecasting that effectively handles uncertain or missing data. Use multiple tasks to learn from both the available data and the uncertainty information, and design a specialized loss function that balances the importance of each task. Evaluate the robustness of this approach under various uncertain or missing data scenarios.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline models without multi-task learning, (2) different uncertainty models (e.g., Gaussian process, Bayesian neural network), (3) traditional robust forecasting methods (e.g., interpolation, extrapolation)
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: The multi-task learning approach will improve the robustness of satellite image time series forecasting under uncertain or missing data, but the selection of relevant tasks and loss functions requires careful consideration. The integration of uncertainty models will provide a promising direction for robust forecasting, but requires careful tuning of model hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE:  Modulating a Video-Capable Multimodal Large Language Model with Temporal Awareness for Scene Change Dynamics
PROPOSAL: Enhance the video-capable multimodal large language model for temporal change description and forecasting by incorporating a temporal awareness module that learns to reason about temporal relationships and scene change dynamics. This module will be designed to attend to key events and patterns over time, and generate more accurate and informative descriptions of scene change. Evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on various scene change description and forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline model without temporal awareness, (2) different attention mechanisms for temporal awareness, (3) traditional multimodal fusion methods
COST: 3030

The research project is now complete. A total of 8 proposals have been developed, covering various aspects of satellite image time series forecasting and scene change description. The proposed approaches include modulating a video-capable multimodal large language model, temporally consistent satellite image forecasting, long-range temporal dependency perspective, scene change explanation, cross-domain adaptation, evaluating temporal consistency, multimodal fusion, and robust forecasting under uncertain or missing data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Updating Different Model Components on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment where we update different components of a pre-trained forecasting model online, such as the final prediction layer, adapters attached to the model's input or output, and the entire model, on multiple real-world benchmarks including traffic flow, electricity consumption, and weather forecasting datasets. We will use online gradient descent (OGD) to update the models and measure their performance using metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE). We will also investigate the effect of updating different model components on the model's ability to adapt to concept drift.
CONTROLS: Frozen base model with no adapter update, basic OGD with all parameters updated
COST: 30,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that updating the final prediction layer and adapters attached to the model's input or output leads to more stable and accurate online forecasting performance compared to updating the entire model, but that the best updating strategy depends on the specific forecasting task and dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Performance of Online Gradient Descent with Delayed Feedback in Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will modify the online gradient descent (OGD) update scheme to account for delayed feedback in multi-step forecasting and evaluate its performance on a set of real-world benchmarks, including traffic flow and electricity consumption forecasting datasets. We will compare the modified OGD scheme to the standard OGD scheme and other methods that account for delayed feedback, such as gradient aggregation with past samples. We will measure performance using metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE).
CONTROLS: Standard OGD, gradient aggregation with past samples
COST: 35,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the modified OGD scheme with delayed feedback leads to improved performance in multi-step forecasting compared to the standard OGD scheme, but may have higher variance due to the additional computational cost of delayed feedback.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing the Robustness of Online Time Series Forecasting Methods to Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the robustness of different online time series forecasting methods to concept drift using synthetic and real-world datasets with varying degrees of concept drift. We will compare the performance of methods such as online gradient descent (OGD), gradient aggregation with past samples, and experience replay to concept drift. We will measure performance using metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE).
CONTROLS: OGD, gradient aggregation with past samples, experience replay
COST: 45,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that experience replay and gradient aggregation with past samples are more robust to concept drift than OGD, but that the most effective method will depend on the specific characteristics of the concept drift.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: REVISED: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Experience Replay for Concept Drift in Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will modify proposal 3 to focus specifically on evaluating the effectiveness of experience replay for concept drift in multi-step forecasting. We will introduce a new concept drift scenario where the underlying relationship between input and output changes over time, and evaluate the performance of experience replay with and without gradient aggregation with past samples. We will also compare the performance to a baseline method that uses standard online gradient descent (OGD).
CONTROLS: Standard OGD, experience replay with gradient aggregation, experience replay without gradient aggregation
COST: 40,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that experience replay with gradient aggregation performs better than experience replay alone in handling concept drift, but both methods will have lower performance than standard OGD in the absence of concept drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Dynamic Regret in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will provide a theoretical analysis of the dynamic regret in online time series forecasting, focusing on the impact of delayed feedback and concept drift on the regret bounds. We will derive regret bounds for online gradient descent (OGD) with and without gradient aggregation, and for experience replay with and without gradient aggregation. We will also investigate the impact of the number of steps, the variance of the gradient estimator, and the magnitude of the concept drift on the regret bounds.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 60,000 GPU-hours (note: this is a theoretical proposal, so it does not require any actual computations)
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the regret bounds for online gradient descent with gradient aggregation are tighter than those for standard OGD, and that the regret bounds for experience replay with gradient aggregation are tighter than those for experience replay alone. However, the actual performance of these methods may deviate from the predicted regret bounds due to the complexity of the time series forecasting problem.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED: Investigating the Impact of Updating Different Model Components on Online Time Series Forecasting with Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: We will modify proposal 1 to investigate the impact of updating different model components on online time series forecasting with concept drift. We will introduce a new concept drift scenario where the underlying relationship between input and output changes over time, and evaluate the performance of updating different model components, such as the final prediction layer, adapters attached to the model's input or output, and the entire model, on online gradient descent (OGD) with and without gradient aggregation. We will also compare the performance to a baseline method that uses standard online gradient descent (OGD) with no updating.
CONTROLS: Standard OGD with no updating, OGD with gradient aggregation, OGD with updating final prediction layer, OGD with updating adapters, OGD with updating entire model
COST: 100,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that updating the final prediction layer and adapters attached to the model's input or output leads to more stable and accurate online forecasting performance compared to updating the entire model, especially in the presence of concept drift.

TITLE: Investigation of Lower-Bounded Optimization for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of lower-bounded optimization techniques for online time series forecasting, where we constrain the updates of the model parameters to be within a certain bounded region to prevent overfitting. We will compare the performance of lower-bounded optimization to standard online gradient descent (OGD) and other optimization methods, such as gradient aggregation with past samples, on real-world time series forecasting datasets.
CONTROLS: Standard OGD, gradient aggregation with past samples, experience replay
COST: 120,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that lower-bounded optimization leads to improved performance and stabler updates compared to standard OGD and other optimization methods, but may require careful tuning of the bounding hyperparameters.

TITLE: A New Adaptive Loss Function for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will propose a new adaptive loss function for online time series forecasting that adjusts the loss function based on the uncertainty in the model predictions and the distribution of the temporal dynamics in the data. We will compare the performance of the proposed adaptive loss function to standard loss functions, such as mean squared error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE), on real-world time series forecasting datasets.
CONTROLS: MSE, MAE, proposed adaptive loss function
COST: 150,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the proposed adaptive loss function leads to improved performance and better handling of concept drift compared to standard loss functions, especially when the distribution of the temporal dynamics in the data is complex.

TITLE: Graph-Based Methods for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of graph-based methods for online time series forecasting, where we construct a graph to represent the temporal relationships between time series data and use graph neural networks (GNNs) to forecasts future values. We will compare the performance of GNNs to traditional forecasting models, such as ARIMA and LSTM, on real-world time series forecasting datasets.
CONTROLS: ARIMA, LSTM, GNN
COST: 210,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that GNNs lead to improved performance and better handling of complex temporal relationships in the data compared to traditional forecasting models, but may require careful tuning of the graph structure and hyperparameters.

TITLE: A Domain-Invariant Online Time Series Forecasting Framework
PROPOSAL: We will propose a new domain-invariant online time series forecasting framework that learns to adapt to changing temporal dynamics and concept drift in a multi-task learning setting. We will use a proxy-based method to learn a domain-invariant representation of the data and use it to develop a robust online forecasting model that can handle concept drift across multiple datasets.
CONTROLS: Standard online gradient descent (OGD), our proposed domain-invariant online time series forecasting framework
COST: 300,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the proposed domain-invariant online time series forecasting framework leads to improved performance and better handling of concept drift across multiple datasets compared to standard OGD, and that the framework can be used as a generalizable solution for online time series forecasting tasks across different domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Heterogeneous Multimodal Encoder Aggregation for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Design an architecture-agnostic method for aggregating the representations of multiple heterogeneous encoders for visual document retrieval. This method, called "HeteroRank," would create a weighted sum of the final vector representations from each encoder, allowing for efficient combination of signals from different models. The weights would be learned during training from the aggregated representations and relevance labels. For a primary vision-centric encoder and a lightweight dense text retriever, HeteroRank would output a joint embedding that captures the complementary strengths of both models.
CONTROLS: Compare HeteroRank with a naive late-interaction baseline (simply concatenating the outputs of the two encoders) and with the current best vision-centric retriever on the dataset.
COST: 10800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HeteroRank outperforms the late-interaction baseline by 10% in recall@10, with similar latency and index memory footprint, and compares favorably to the current best vision-centric retriever, but with a smaller, lighter models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rank-Level Aggregation for Retrieve-Rerank in Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate a rank-level aggregation approach for retrieving documents with a primary vision-centric encoder and then reranking them with a lightweight dense text retriever. This method, called "RankPool," would first compute the retrieval scores of the primary encoder and then use the reranker's scores to reorder and refine the top-ranked documents. To handle the heterogeneity of the two models, RankPool would learn a lightweight, model-agnostic reranking model that accounts for the differences in representation spaces between the encoders.
CONTROLS: Compare RankPool with the naive late-interaction baseline and with HeteroRank on different datasets and under various evaluation metrics.
COST: 16200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: RankPool significantly reduces the latency of the overall retrieval pipeline while achieving competitive recall metrics with HeteroRank, but may not adapt as well to non-overlapping evaluation modules.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Role of Modality Gap in Vision-Centric Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Analyze the impact of modality gap, or the difference in representation spaces between vision and text modalities, on the performance of primary vision-centric encoders in multimodal retrieval. This study will examine how different methods of bridging the modality gap, such as multi-modal pre-training or modality-invariant bottleneck features, affect the retrieval performance on public benchmarks for visual document retrieval.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of various vision-centric encoders with and without modality gap bridging techniques to the simple late-interaction baseline.
COST: 21600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By investigating the role of modality gap in vision-centric encoding methods, the findings could provide insights into why the paradigm of hybrid retrieval might be beneficial for vision-centric multimodal encoders and highlight the potential limitations of solely-reliance on dense and image multimodal retrieves in certain circumstances.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Feasibility of Weakly-Supervised Learning for Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Explore the possibility of using weak supervision, such as relevance labels only for a limited portion of the dataset, to improve the performance of hybrid multimodal retrievers. This study will investigate the impact of weak supervision on the learned weights of the HeteroRank and RankPool methods and compare their performance to those trained with full supervision.
CONTROLS: Compare the retrieval performance of hybrid retrievers trained with and without weak supervision on both public benchmarks and in-domain datasets.
COST: 24300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By successfully leveraging weak supervision, the hybrid retrievers could achieve competitive performance with fully-supervised counterparts but with reduced labeling efforts, thereby making them more practical for real-world deployments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Computational Complexity Analysis for Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the computational complexity of hybrid multimodal retrieval methods, particularly for HeteroRank and RankPool. This analysis will provide insights into the scalability of these methods and help identify potential optimizations to reduce latency and index memory footprint.
CONTROLS: Compare the theoretical complexity analysis with empirical measurements of HeteroRank and RankPool on various datasets and scales.
COST: 27000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The computational complexity analysis will reveal bottlenecks in the hybrid retrieval methods and provide actionable recommendations for optimizing their implementation, making them more practical for large-scale deployments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Different Indexing Techniques on Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of various indexing techniques, such as hierarchical and approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexing, on the efficiency of hybrid multimodal retrieval methods. This study will compare the retrieval performance and computational efficiency of HeteroRank and RankPool when using different indexing techniques and provide recommendations for optimal indexing configurations.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of various indexing techniques with and without parallelization on multi-GPU and multi-node systems.
COST: 32400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By optimizing the indexing strategy, hybrid retrievers can achieve significant speedups without compromising recall performance, making them more suitable for large-scale deployment in real-world pipelines.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Impact of Textual Query Complexity on Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval
